fg-muted.note: Also the colour of status the user reads but cannot click.

fg-disabled.note: The only way to say disabled. Never opacity.

success-500.note: Ramp synthesized for display; the project defines only the 500 step.

warning-500.note: Ramp synthesized for display; the project defines only the 500 step, used as a solid text colour and as a 15% tint with a 30% ring.

danger-500.note: Ramp synthesized for display; the project defines only the 500 step.

info-500.note: Defined in tokens.css but currently unused; informational markers take accent-300.

focus.note: Theme-dependent (--focus): accent-400 on dark, accent-600 on light. No single ramp step clears 3:1 against both themes' surfaces.

display.purpose: The largest type in the app (18px): a modal's own title, an empty-state headline. No text-xl or text-2xl exists.

title.purpose: Section and dialog headings at body size (14px), separated by weight and colour rather than scale.

body.purpose: The working size (14px): track titles, cell values, button labels, inputs. Monospace, so columns align.

prose.purpose: Inter, opted into only for real sentences — help text under a setting, a release note, an explanation in a dialog.

label.purpose: 12px monospace for secondary values, tallies and pills; 11px/10px exist for progress detail and corner badges.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Quietest lift; defined in tokens, rarely needed.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Default for a popover or dialog panel (filter menu, column menu).

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: The docked header and larger floating panels; written as shadow-lg shadow-black/40.

shadows.name: overlay-backdrop
shadows.purpose: Modal backdrop at z-50, portalled into document.body, page scroll-locked.

motion.name: animate-fade-in
motion.purpose: Content appearing: view switch, filter or sort change, loaded covers, splash text.

motion.name: animate-fade-out
motion.purpose: The splash handing over to the app.

motion.name: animate-skeleton
motion.purpose: Placeholder pulse — opacity only, never a gradient sweep.

motion.name: animate-eq
motion.purpose: The four logo bars bouncing like an equalizer on the splash.

motion.name: dock
motion.purpose: The sticky header and filter bar docking on scroll.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: An overflowing title scrolls only while its row is hovered; two copies, -50% shift.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Mandatory. Every animation is switched off in index.css and content is complete in its final state.

breakpoints.name: table-min
breakpoints.note: The track table's own min-width (min-w-[95rem]); it scrolls horizontally inside its container rather than reflowing.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one thing to do next in a given context — convert, scan, download.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:36px; padding:0 16px; border:none; border-radius:8px; background:var(--color-accent-600,#574BC0); color:var(--fg,#F6F6F8); font-family:JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size:14px; font-weight:500; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color .15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover:enabled { background:var(--color-accent-500,#6A5FD6); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent-400,#8177E0); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background:var(--surface-2,#201F28); color:var(--fg-disabled,#5A5A66); cursor:default; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Quiet until touched: a hairline outline that picks up the accent on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:36px; padding:0 12px; border:1px solid var(--border-strong,#343440); border-radius:8px; background:transparent; color:var(--fg-muted,#B7B7C0); font-family:JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size:14px; font-weight:400; cursor:pointer; transition:border-color .15s ease-out,color .15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover:enabled { border-color:var(--color-accent-500,#6A5FD6); color:var(--color-accent-400,#8177E0); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent-400,#8177E0); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { border-color:var(--border,#292933); color:var(--fg-disabled,#5A5A66); cursor:default; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: Square at the same 36px, never a bare glyph. The dot marks something unread; the label says what.
components.css: .ds-btn-icon { position:relative; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:36px; width:36px; flex-shrink:0; border:1px solid var(--border-strong,#343440); border-radius:8px; background:transparent; color:var(--fg-muted,#B7B7C0); cursor:pointer; transition:border-color .15s ease-out,color .15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-icon:hover { border-color:var(--color-accent-500,#6A5FD6); color:var(--color-accent-400,#8177E0); } .ds-btn-icon:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent-400,#8177E0); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-icon-dot { position:absolute; right:-4px; top:-4px; height:10px; width:10px; border-radius:9999px; background:var(--color-accent-500,#6A5FD6); box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--bg,#100F14); }

components.name: Segmented Navigation
components.description: The Library/Bandcamp switch: an outlined group with 36px tabs, exactly one active.
components.css: .ds-nav { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:4px; padding:2px; border:1px solid var(--border-strong,#343440); border-radius:12px; } .ds-nav-tab { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:36px; padding:0 12px; border:none; border-radius:8px; background:transparent; color:var(--fg-muted,#B7B7C0); font-family:JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size:14px; cursor:pointer; transition:color .15s ease-out,background-color .15s ease-out; } .ds-nav-tab:hover { color:var(--fg,#F6F6F8); } .ds-nav-tab:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--color-accent-400,#8177E0); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-nav-tab--active { background:rgb(87 75 192 / .2); color:var(--color-accent-200,#BCB6F1); }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: The border is the focus indicator — no glow, no ring. Same 8 px corner as every button.
components.css: .ds-input { width:224px; padding:6px 12px; border:1px solid var(--border-strong,#343440); border-radius:8px; background:var(--surface-2,#201F28); color:var(--fg,#F6F6F8); font-family:JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size:14px;  transition:border-color .15s ease-out; } .ds-input::placeholder { color:var(--fg-subtle,#8C8C98); } .ds-input:focus { border-color:var(--color-accent-500,#6A5FD6); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--focus,#8177E0); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-input:disabled { color:var(--fg-subtle,#8C8C98); }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: The tinted-ring triple: 15% background, solid text, 30% ring. Colour means compatibility, never decoration.
components.html: → AIFF 44.1 kHz runs on CDJ E-8305 risk
components.css: .ds-pill { display:inline-block; border-radius:9999px; padding:2px 8px; font-family:JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size:12px; } .ds-pill--warning { background:rgb(245 166 35 / .15); color:var(--color-warning-500,#F5A623); box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(245 166 35 / .3); } .ds-pill--success { background:rgb(34 178 122 / .15); color:var(--color-success-500,#22B27A); box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(34 178 122 / .3); } .ds-pill--danger { background:rgb(229 72 77 / .15); color:var(--color-danger-500,#E5484D); box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(229 72 77 / .3); }

Kettenkarussell·Insecurity Guard
96 kHz · 24-bit
components.css: .ds-row { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; height:64px; padding:0 16px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--border,#292933); color:var(--fg,#F6F6F8); font-family:JetBrains Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size:14px; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color .15s ease-out; } .ds-row:hover { background:var(--surface-2,#201F28); } .ds-row-cover { height:40px; width:40px; flex-shrink:0; border-radius:4px; background:var(--surface-2,#201F28); } .ds-row-main { min-width:0; flex:1; } .ds-row-title { overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; } .ds-row-meta { display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:6px; font-size:12px; color:var(--fg-muted,#B7B7C0); } .ds-row-meta-first { min-width:0; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; } .ds-row-sep { flex-shrink:0; color:var(--fg-subtle,#8C8C98); } .ds-row-meta-last { min-width:0; flex-shrink:999; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; color:var(--fg-subtle,#8C8C98); } .ds-row-tech { flex-shrink:0; font-size:12px; color:var(--fg-subtle,#8C8C98); } .ds-row-status { flex-shrink:0; display:flex; align-items:center; color:var(--color-warning-500,#F5A623); }

components.css: .ds-progress { height:6px; width:100%; overflow:hidden; border-radius:9999px; background:var(--surface-2,#201F28); } .ds-progress-fill { height:100%; border-radius:9999px; background:var(--color-accent-500,#6A5FD6); transition:width .3s ease-out; }

narrative.overview:
rekord-lib looks like a piece of studio equipment, not like a music app. The surface is near-black, the type is monospace almost everywhere, and the numbers that matter — 44.1 kHz, 24-bit, 128.0 BPM, AIFF — sit in columns that line up because the font makes them line up. One violet accent runs through the instrument and marks the signal: the waveform, the progress bar, the primary action. Everything else is graphite.

The mood is calm, precise, incorruptible. Nothing pushes, nothing celebrates. The interface's job is to state a verdict about a file the user cannot inspect by ear — whether a CDJ will refuse it — and a readout that exaggerates is worse than no readout. So colour is spent on meaning, never on mood: green means ready, amber means it needs work, red means a player will refuse it, violet means this is the thing to act on. A screen with no problems is a screen with almost no colour in it, and that is the intended resting state.

Controls are quiet until touched. At rest a button is a hairline and a label; the track list dominates and the chrome recedes. On hover the border or the icon picks up the accent, and that is the whole gesture. Depth works the same way: three surface tones carry the layering, and a shadow appears only under something that genuinely floats. The two things this must never look like are an enterprise data grid and a playful consumer app.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default (data-theme="dark" on <html>); light is a full, supported theme, not an afterthought.
Monospace as the default voice of the UI — Inter is opted into for prose.
Exactly one accent (violet), and status colour that only ever means compatibility.
Every button 36 px tall, stated as a height and enforced by a test.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, shadows reserved for floating layers.
Compact density: 64 px track rows, px-3 py-2 cells, 12 px gaps.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus is one ring, defined once in index.css as :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px } — never per component, never suppressed. --focus is theme-dependent because no single accent step clears 3:1 on both themes. The rules are unlayered so no Tailwind outline-* utility can outrank them, and designRules.test.ts fails on any outline-none.

rules.name: The Semantic Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red only ever describe compatibility state. A status colour used because it looks good is a defect. A build label that is merely a heads-up ("Beta") takes the accent, not amber.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet is the only brand colour. No second accent, no gradient, no glow — including as a skeleton shimmer, which is why placeholders pulse their opacity instead.

rules.name: The Opacity Rule
rules.body: Never express disabled with opacity; it multiplies with the content's own colour and lands on a different grey in every control. Say it in colour (bg-surface-2 / border-border / text-fg-disabled) and guard every hover with enabled:.

rules.name: The Tinted-Ring Rule
rules.body: A status surface is a 15% tint of the status colour, a 30% ring of the same hue, and the solid hue as text — a ring rather than a border, because a pill sits inside a row. The opaque --bg-warning/--fg-warning pairs tokens.css once carried were never used and were removed in 0.9.1, so there is no text-fg-warning utility: a colour utility no token defines generates nothing rather than failing.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Sentence case everywhere. No Title Case, no ALL CAPS — including for data that arrives lowercase, which is not made to shout by an uppercase class. Enforced over the source by src/styles/designRules.test.ts.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 regular and 500 medium, nothing else. A heading separates itself by weight and colour, not by a third level. Enforced over the source by src/styles/designRules.test.ts.

rules.name: The Mono-Default Rule
rules.body: Never set a value, label, control or table cell in Inter; reach for font-sans exactly when writing a sentence the user reads once.

rules.name: The Falling-Order Truncation Rule
rules.body: When a line carries several values, the last one gives way first: min-w-0 truncate on both, shrink-[999] on the one that goes first. Never a fixed width.

rules.name: The Downward Menu Rule
rules.body: A menu opens downward and above the header: right-0 top-full mt-2 z-40. The header is a 64 px sticky bar at z-30, so bottom-full opens off the top of the window. Layer stack: filter bar 20, header 30, menus 40, modal 50.

rules.name: The Tone-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: If two things need telling apart, move one to the next surface tone. Add a shadow only when the element actually floats over content.

rules.name: The 36 px Rule
rules.body: Every button is h-9 (36 px), stated as a height and never derived from padding; icon-only buttons are square at the same number. buttonShape.test.ts enforces height and corner over the source.

dos: Do take every colour from src/styles/tokens.css — semantic tokens for surfaces, text and lines; accent-* for brand, action and progress; the three status hues for compatibility only.
Do state a button's height as h-9 and make an icon-only button h-9 w-9.
Do default to font-mono and opt into font-sans only for sentences.
Do express disabled in colour (disabled:bg-surface-2, disabled:text-fg-disabled, disabled:border-border) and guard hovers with enabled:.
Do open menus with right-0 top-full mt-2 z-40.
Do give a new animation a token in tokens.css and add it to the prefers-reduced-motion block in index.css.
Do let the later value truncate first when a line carries several (shrink-[999]).
Do carry meaning in text as well as colour — a coloured dot is 10 px of hue and not a message, so the tooltip and the accessible name say the level.
donts: Don't write a focus style on a component, or suppress the shared one with outline-none — see the One Ring Rule.
Don't use a Tailwind default palette (neutral-*, sky-*, emerald-*) or a raw hex in a component.
Don't use a status colour decoratively, or a second accent, or a gradient or glow anywhere — including a shimmer sweep across a skeleton.
Don't derive a control's height from padding, and don't put a bare glyph where a 36 px square button belongs.
Don't set body text in mono's place or set a value, label or table cell in Inter.
Don't use Title Case, ALL CAPS, or weight 600/700.
Don't stack a shadow on a bordered surface to create depth — move it to the next surface tone instead.
Don't animate list rows; animate the container, because the table renders only its visible rows and a per-row animation refires on every scroll.
Don't make it look like an enterprise data grid — no grey toolbars, no zebra striping, no border around every cell, no default framework blue.
Don't make it look like a playful consumer app — no illustrations, no coachmarks, no emoji in the UI, no encouraging copy. The app states facts about files.
Don't write a colour utility no token defines (text-fg-warning, bg-bg-danger) — Tailwind generates nothing for it and the element silently keeps the inherited colour.
